# Plakar

> Plakar is an open-source backup tool that provides end-to-end encrypted,
> deduplicated backups. It is powered by Kloset, an immutable data store engine
> that handles chunking, deduplication, compression, and encryption, and
> represents all backed-up data internally as a virtual filesystem. Plakar's
> integration model allows any data source, storage backend, or restore
> destination to be supported through pluggable connectors, making it adaptable
> to files, databases, object storage, SaaS, and more. It is designed for a
> minimal memory footprint and scales to petabyte-scale infrastructure. Plakar
> Control Plane (PCP) is the enterprise product built on top of Plakar.

Every page on plakar.io has a Markdown version. Add `index.md` to the end of a page URL to read it (for example `https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/installation/index.md`). The links in this file point to these Markdown versions where one exists.

## Overview

- [Quick Start](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/first-backup/index.md): Quick introduction to installing Plakar and running your first backup.
- [How Plakar Works](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/explanations/how-plakar-works/index.md): Architectural overview of Plakar and Kloset.
- [What is Kloset](https://www.plakar.io/posts/2025-04-29/kloset-the-immutable-data-store/index.md): Kloset's immutable storage model, chunking, encryption, and snapshot architecture.
- [What is Plakar Control Plane](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/intro/overview/index.md): Overview of PCP, the enterprise product built on top of Plakar.

## Install

Plakar is a command-line tool, `plakar`. Integrations such as S3 or SFTP are separate packages that you install with `plakar pkg add` (see [Managing Packages](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/guides/managing-packages/index.md)). Pick one install method, then run `plakar version` to check it. Full instructions with copy-paste commands: [Installation](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/installation/index.md).

- Homebrew: `brew install plakarkorp/tap/plakar` (Plakar tap, recommended by the docs) or `brew install plakar` (Homebrew core, which may not always have the latest release).
- Debian and Ubuntu (apt): add the signing key from https://plakar.io/dist/keys/plakar-packages.gpg and the repository `deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/plakar.gpg] https://plakar.io/dist/repos/deb/ stable main`, then run `sudo apt-get install plakar`.
- Fedora and other RPM systems (dnf): add the repository `https://plakar.io/dist/repos/rpm/$basearch/` with the same signing key, then run `sudo dnf install plakar`.
- Go toolchain: `go install github.com/PlakarKorp/plakar@latest`. Since v1.1.8, building Plakar requires Go 1.26.10 or later.
- Arch Linux: `yay -S plakar` (AUR).
- Pre-built binaries and packages for macOS, Linux, FreeBSD, OpenBSD and Windows, with SHA256 checksums: [Download page](https://www.plakar.io/download/) (HTML only, no Markdown version) or [GitHub releases](https://github.com/PlakarKorp/plakar/releases).
- Docker: The plakar repository includes a [Dockerfile](https://github.com/PlakarKorp/plakar/blob/main/Dockerfile) that you can build with `docker build`.

## Automate backups

Plakar 1.1.x has no built-in scheduler (the `plakar scheduler` and `plakar agent` commands of 1.0.x were removed). To run backups on a schedule, call `plakar backup` from the scheduler your operating system already has. On Linux, systemd timers are the recommended pattern: they log to the journal and catch up on runs missed while the machine was off. cron, launchd (macOS) and Windows Task Scheduler also work.

- [Scheduling Backups](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/guides/setup-scheduler-daily-backups/index.md): prerequisites for every scheduler, including how to supply the store passphrase without a prompt (`passphrase` or `passphrase_cmd` in the store configuration, the `-keyfile` flag, or the `PLAKAR_PASSPHRASE` environment variable).
- [Linux: cron and systemd timers](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/guides/setup-scheduler-daily-backups/linux/index.md): example crontab line, and `plakar-backup.service` plus `plakar-backup.timer` units with `Persistent=true`.
- [macOS: launchd](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/guides/setup-scheduler-daily-backups/macos/index.md)
- [Windows: Task Scheduler](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/guides/setup-scheduler-daily-backups/windows/index.md)

The command to schedule is the same everywhere. Use the absolute path to the binary, because schedulers run with a minimal `PATH`:

```bash
/usr/local/bin/plakar at @mybackups backup -check /var/www
```

`-check` runs a full integrity check after the backup. `plakar backup` exits 0 on success and non-zero on failure, so alert on the exit status. Plakar Control Plane adds a built-in scheduler, see [Scheduling](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/index.md), and can back up every resource of a cloud account automatically, see [Automating Backups from an Inventory](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/automated-backups/index.md).

## Restore

Reference: [plakar restore](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-restore/index.md).

```bash
plakar at <store> restore [-to <directory> | -to @<destination>] [<snapshotID>[:<path>]]
```

- `-to <directory>` sets the base directory for the restored files. Without `-to`, files are restored into the current working directory. Original paths are kept under the base directory: in the quickstart, restoring a snapshot of `/home/user/Documents` with `-to /home/user/restored` recreates the files under `/home/user/restored/Documents/`.
- `-to @<name>` restores into a configured destination connector instead of the local filesystem, for example an S3 bucket: `plakar restore -to @s3target abc123`.
- `<snapshotID>:<path>` restores only that path from the snapshot (partial restore): `plakar restore -to /mnt/ abc123:/etc/apache2`. Without `:<path>`, the whole snapshot is restored. Without a snapshot ID, Plakar restores the current working directory from the last matching snapshot.
- Use the short snapshot ID printed by `plakar backup` and `plakar ls`.
- File permissions and ownership are restored unless you pass `-skip-permissions`.

To find what to restore: [plakar ls](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-ls/index.md) lists snapshots and their contents, [plakar locate](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-locate/index.md) finds files by name in snapshots, [plakar cat](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-cat/index.md) prints a single file without restoring it, and [plakar mount](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-mount/index.md) mounts snapshots as a read-only filesystem.

## When to Use Plakar

Reach for Plakar when the job is to create, manage, verify, or restore encrypted, deduplicated backups, either from the command line or through Plakar Control Plane. Best-fit jobs:

- Back up and restore filesystems, databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL/MariaDB), S3-compatible object storage, and SaaS data through pluggable connectors.
- Keep immutable, end-to-end encrypted, deduplicated snapshots in a Kloset store, then verify integrity ([`plakar check`](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-check/index.md)) and restore ([`plakar restore`](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-restore/index.md)) to the same or another destination.
- Synchronize Kloset stores across locations with [`plakar sync`](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-sync/index.md), using push or pull architectures for offsite or redundant copies.
- Run at minimal memory footprint and petabyte scale, on a single host or a centralized backup server.
- Manage backups centrally with Plakar Control Plane (PCP): a self-hosted web interface, centralized scheduling, SLA, and inventory management, deployed as a virtual appliance in your own infrastructure.

Plakar is not a file-sync tool, a general object-storage client, or a versioning system. Use it when you need recoverable, verifiable backups.

How an agent should use Plakar:

- Drive it through the `plakar` command-line interface. Start with [First Backup](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/first-backup/index.md) and the [Command-Line Syntax](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/command-line-syntax/index.md) reference; the full command list is in the Commands section below.
- Every documentation page has a machine-readable Markdown version at its `.../index.md` URL, as linked throughout this file.

## Plakar Community Docs

Plakar Community version is open-source and free to use. Documentation is versioned to match releases. Replace the version segment in any `/docs/community/` URL to switch versions. Only use these four version identifiers. No others exist.

- [main (development)](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/main/index.md): Bleeding-edge branch, may be unstable.
- [v1.1.0 (latest stable)](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/index.md): Latest stable release, recommended for all users.
- [v1.0.6](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.0.6/index.md): Previous stable release.
- [v1.0.5](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.0.5/index.md): Previous stable release.

- [Installation](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/installation/index.md): How to install Plakar on your system.
- [First Backup](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/first-backup/index.md): End-to-end walkthrough: create a Kloset store, run a backup, list snapshots, verify integrity, and restore.
- [Synchronize Kloset stores](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/synchronize-copies/index.md): Duplicate a Kloset store to another location using `plakar sync`.
- [Backup Non-Filesystem Data](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/quickstart/backup-non-filesystem-data/index.md): Back up an S3 bucket using a configured source, and restore it to an S3 destination.

- [MySQL: SQL Dump](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/guides/mysql/sqldump/index.md): Logical SQL dump backup for MySQL and MariaDB using the MySQL integration.

### Explanations

- [Should You Pull or Push Backups](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/explanations/should-you-pull-or-push-backups/index.md): How to decide between push and pull backup architectures, and how Plakar supports both.
- [How Many Kloset Stores Should I Have](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/explanations/how-many-kloset-stores/index.md): How to decide between a single shared store or multiple stores based on deduplication boundaries, encryption scope, and operational needs.
- [Why Several Copies](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/explanations/why-several-copies/index.md): Why multiple backup copies matter and the 3-2-1 backup strategy.
- [Why Should I Back Up My SaaS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/explanations/why-should-i-backup-my-saas/index.md): Why SaaS availability is not the same as data protection, and why independent backups are necessary under the shared responsibility model.
- [How Maintenance Works](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/explanations/how-maintenance-works/index.md): How Plakar reclaims storage after snapshot deletion: chunking, packfiles, garbage collection, and the grace period.

### Integrations

Each integration tells Plakar how to interact with a specific storage system in up to three ways: as a **source** (read data to back up), as a **store** (host a Kloset store), or as a **destination** (restore data back to that system).

- [S3](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/s3/index.md): S3-compatible object storage (store, source, destination).
- [SFTP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/sftp/index.md): SFTP/SSH-accessible servers (store, source, destination).
- [HTTP(S)](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/http/index.md): HTTP/HTTPS endpoint for stores exposed by `plakar server` (store).
- [Azure Blob Storage](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/azblob/index.md): Azure Blob Storage containers (store, source, destination).
- [Google Cloud Storage](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/gcs/index.md): Google Cloud Storage buckets (store, source, destination).
- [OCI Registry](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/oci/index.md): OCI registry as a Kloset store backend (store).
- [WebDAV](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/webdav/index.md): WebDAV remotes (source, destination).
- [FTP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/ftp/index.md): Remote directories over FTP (source, destination).
- [SMB / CIFS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/smb/index.md): SMB shares (source, destination).
- [NFS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/nfs/index.md): NFS exports (source, destination).
- [PostgreSQL](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/postgres/index.md): PostgreSQL databases, logical dumps and physical cluster backups (source, destination).
- [MySQL / MariaDB](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/mysql/index.md): MySQL and MariaDB databases (source, destination).
- [MongoDB](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/mongodb/index.md): MongoDB databases (source, destination).
- [Microsoft SQL Server](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/mssql/index.md): SQL Server on a live Windows system (source, destination).
- [Microsoft Active Directory](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/msad/index.md): Windows System State of Active Directory Domain Controllers (source, destination).
- [Windows VSS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/vss/index.md): Live Windows systems through Volume Shadow Copy Service (source, destination).
- [IMAP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/imap/index.md): Mailboxes over IMAP (source, destination).
- [VMware](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/vmware/index.md): VMware vSphere virtual machines (source, destination).
- [Proxmox](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/proxmox/index.md): Proxmox VMs and containers via vzdump (source, destination).
- [Scaleway](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/scaleway/index.md): Scaleway instances, block volumes and Secret Manager secrets (source, destination).
- [OpenStack](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/openstack/index.md): OpenStack Nova servers and Cinder volumes (source, destination).
- [Kubernetes](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/kubernetes/index.md): Kubernetes cluster resources, manifests, and persistent volumes (source).
- [OpenShift](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/openshift/index.md): OpenShift manifests (configuration only), PVC contents and OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines (source, destination).
- [etcd](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/etcd/index.md): etcd cluster snapshots (source).
- [Notion](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/notion/index.md): Notion workspace via the Notion API (source, destination).
- [Dropbox](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/dropbox/index.md): Dropbox via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [iCloud Drive](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/iclouddrive/index.md): iCloud Drive via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [Koofr](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/koofr/index.md): Koofr via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [Google Drive](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/googledrive/index.md): Google Drive via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [OneDrive](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/onedrive/index.md): OneDrive via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [OpenDrive](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/opendrive/index.md): OpenDrive via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [Proton Drive](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/protondrive/index.md): Proton Drive via Rclone (store, source, destination).
- [TAR](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/tar/index.md): Import TAR archives into a Kloset store (source).
- [STDIO](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/integrations/stdio/index.md): Back up from stdin and restore to stdout or stderr (source, destination).

### References

- [Command-Line Syntax](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/command-line-syntax/index.md): Global flags, environment variables, and output formats.
- [Go Kloset SDK](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/go-kloset-sdk/index.md): Reference for the Go Kloset SDK used to build custom Plakar integrations: importer, exporter, and storage connector interfaces, packaging, and a complete example. Connectors talk to Plakar over gRPC, so integrations can be written in any language, but Go is the only language with an official SDK.

### Commands

- [plakar archive](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-archive/index.md): Create an archive from a Plakar snapshot.
- [plakar backup](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-backup/index.md): Create a new snapshot in a Kloset store.
- [plakar cat](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-cat/index.md): Display file contents from a Plakar snapshot.
- [plakar check](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-check/index.md): Check data integrity in a Kloset repository.
- [plakar create](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-create/index.md): Create a new Kloset repository.
- [plakar destination](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-destination/index.md): Manage Plakar restore destination configuration.
- [plakar diag](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-diag/index.md): Display detailed information about Plakar internal structures.
- [plakar diff](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-diff/index.md): Show differences between files in a Plakar snapshots.
- [plakar digest](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-digest/index.md): Compute digests for files in a Plakar snapshot.
- [plakar dup](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-dup/index.md): Duplicates an existing snapshot with a different ID.
- [plakar info](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-info/index.md): Display detailed information about internal structures.
- [plakar locate](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-locate/index.md): Find filenames in a Plakar snapshot.
- [plakar login](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-login/index.md): Authenticate to Plakar services.
- [plakar logout](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-logout/index.md): Log out from Plakar services.
- [plakar ls](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-ls/index.md): List snapshots and their contents in a Kloset repository.
- [plakar maintenance](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-maintenance/index.md): Remove unused data from a Plakar repository.
- [plakar mount](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-mount/index.md): Mount Plakar snapshots as read-only filesystem.
- [plakar pkg add](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-add/index.md): Install Plakar plugins.
- [plakar pkg build](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-build/index.md): Build Plakar plugins from source.
- [plakar pkg create](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-create/index.md): Package a plugin.
- [plakar pkg manifest](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-manifest.yaml/index.md): Manifest for plugin assemblation.
- [plakar pkg recipe](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-recipe.yaml/index.md): Recipe to build Plakar plugins from source.
- [plakar pkg rm](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-rm/index.md): Uninstall Plakar plugins.
- [plakar pkg show](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-pkg-show/index.md): Show installed Plakar plugins.
- [plakar policy](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-policy/index.md): Manage Plakar retention policies.
- [plakar prune](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-prune/index.md): Prune snapshots according to a policy.
- [plakar ptar](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-ptar/index.md): Generate a self-contained Kloset archive (.ptar).
- [plakar query](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-query/index.md): Query flags shared among many Plakar subcommands.
- [plakar restore](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-restore/index.md): Restore files from a Plakar snapshot.
- [plakar rm](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-rm/index.md): Remove snapshots from a Plakar repository.
- [plakar server](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-server/index.md): Start a Plakar server.
- [plakar service](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-service/index.md): Manage optional Plakar-connected services.
- [plakar source](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-source/index.md): Manage Plakar backup source configuration.
- [plakar store](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-store/index.md): Manage Plakar store configurations.
- [plakar sync](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-sync/index.md): Synchronize snapshots between Plakar repositories.
- [plakar token create](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-token-create/index.md): Create a token to authenticate to Plakar services.
- [plakar ui](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-ui/index.md): Serve the Plakar web user interface.
- [plakar version](https://www.plakar.io/docs/community/v1.1.0/references/commands/plakar-version/index.md): Display the current Plakar version.

## Plakar Control Plane Docs

Plakar Control Plane is a self-hosted backup management system built on top of Plakar. It adds a web interface, centralized scheduling, SLA, inventory management to Plakar and deployed as a virtual appliance in your own infrastructure.

### Getting Started

- [Control Plane Overview](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/intro/overview/index.md): What the Control Plane is, who it is for and how it works.
- [Installation](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/intro/installation/index.md): Deploy PCP as a virtual appliance on AWS, OVHcloud, Scaleway, Exoscale, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, VMware vSphere or Proxmox VE.
- [Enrollment](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/intro/enrollment/index.md): One-time setup that registers your PCP instance with plakar.io to retrieve your license and enable billing reporting.
- [Signing In](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/intro/signing-in/index.md): Sign in to PCP and select the organization to work in.
- [Billing & Plans](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/intro/billing/index.md): Available plans and pricing for Plakar Control Plane.

### Integrations and Secret Providers

- [Integrations](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/integrations/index.md): Install and manage the integrations that provide inventories, secret providers, sources, stores and destinations.
- [Secret Providers](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/secret-providers/index.md): Resolve credentials from an external secret manager instead of storing them in PCP, and rotate them in one place.
- [Secret Provider: AWS Secrets Manager](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/secret-providers/aws/index.md): Use AWS Secrets Manager as a secret provider.
- [Secret Provider: HashiCorp Vault](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/secret-providers/vault/index.md): Use HashiCorp Vault as a secret provider.
- [Secret Provider: Scaleway Secret Manager](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/secret-providers/scaleway/index.md): Use Scaleway Secret Manager as a secret provider.
- [Secret Provider: GCP Secret Manager](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/secret-providers/gcp/index.md): Use Google Cloud Secret Manager as a secret provider.
- [Secret Provider: OVHcloud Secret Manager](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/secret-providers/ovhcloud/index.md): Use OVHcloud Secret Manager as a secret provider.

### Inventories

- [Inventories](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/index.md): How inventories hold the resources PCP manages, managed and self-managed, and how residency is inherited.
- [Managed Inventories](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/index.md): Inventories that discover resources from a cloud provider or platform.
- [Inventory: AWS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/aws/index.md): Discover AWS resources.
- [Inventory: OVHcloud](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/ovhcloud/index.md): Discover the resources of every project of an OVHcloud account.
- [Inventory: Scaleway](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/scaleway/index.md): Discover the resources of a Scaleway project.
- [Inventory: Google Cloud](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/google-cloud/index.md): Discover Google Cloud resources.
- [Inventory: Kubernetes](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/kubernetes/index.md): Discover the resources of a Kubernetes cluster.
- [Inventory: VMware](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/vmware/index.md): Discover the virtual machines of a vCenter Server.
- [Inventory: OpenStack](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/openstack/index.md): Discover the Nova servers, Cinder volumes, Swift containers and Trove databases of an OpenStack project.
- [Inventory: OpenShift](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/managed/openshift/index.md): Discover the namespaces, PVCs and OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines of an OpenShift cluster.
- [Inventory: Self-managed](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/self-managed/index.md): Add resources by hand or from a CSV file.
- [Configuration Bundles](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/inventories/configuration-bundles/index.md): Share credentials and settings across the resources of an inventory, and auto-create apps.

### Resources

- [Resource Types](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/index.md): Resources, their classification, settings and tags, with links to every supported resource type.
- [Object Storage: S3](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/object-storage/s3/index.md): S3-compatible object storage, including AWS S3, Scaleway, MinIO, etc.
- [Object Storage: Azure Blob Storage](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/object-storage/azblob/index.md): Azure Blob Storage containers.
- [Object Storage: Google Cloud Storage](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/object-storage/gcs/index.md): Google Cloud Storage buckets.
- [Block Storage: Scaleway](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/block-storage/scaleway/index.md): Back up Scaleway block volumes.
- [Block Storage: Kubernetes PVC](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/block-storage/pvc/index.md): Back up and restore Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaims.
- [Block Storage: OpenStack](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/block-storage/openstack/index.md): Back up and restore OpenStack Cinder volumes.
- [Block Storage: OpenShift PVC](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/block-storage/openshift-pvc/index.md): Back up and restore OpenShift PersistentVolumeClaims, through a CSI snapshot or the live volume.
- [Compute: Scaleway](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/scaleway/index.md): Back up and restore Scaleway instances.
- [Compute: VMware](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/vmware/index.md): Back up and restore VMware virtual machines.
- [Compute: Windows VSS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/vss/index.md): Back up and restore Windows systems through Volume Shadow Copy Service.
- [Compute: OpenStack](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/openstack/index.md): Back up OpenStack Nova servers and restore them onto an existing server.
- [Compute: OVHcloud](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/ovhcloud/index.md): Back up and restore OVHcloud compute instances.
- [Compute: Kubernetes VM](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/kubernetes-vm/index.md): Back up and restore KubeVirt virtual machines.
- [Compute: OpenShift](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/openshift/index.md): OpenShift cluster and namespace resources, and OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines.
- [Compute: OpenShift Cluster](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/openshift/cluster/index.md): Back up and restore the manifests (configuration only) of an OpenShift cluster or namespace.
- [Compute: OpenShift VM](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/compute/openshift/vm/index.md): Back up and restore OpenShift Virtualization virtual machines with their disks.
- [Database: Microsoft SQL Server](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/database/mssql/index.md): Back up and restore SQL Server.
- [Database: MySQL](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/database/mysql/index.md): Back up and restore MySQL and MariaDB.
- [Database: PostgreSQL](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/database/postgres/index.md): Back up and restore PostgreSQL.
- [Database: etcd](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/database/etcd/index.md): Back up etcd clusters.
- [Database: MongoDB](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/database/mongodb/index.md): Back up and restore MongoDB.
- [File Storage: SFTP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/file-storage/sftp/index.md): SFTP servers.
- [File Storage: FTP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/file-storage/ftp/index.md): FTP servers.
- [File Storage: WebDAV](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/file-storage/webdav/index.md): WebDAV remotes.
- [File Storage: SMB](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/file-storage/smb/index.md): SMB shares.
- [File Storage: NFS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/file-storage/nfs/index.md): NFS exports.
- [Hypervisor: Proxmox](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/hypervisor/proxmox/index.md): Back up and restore Proxmox VMs and containers.
- [Identity: Microsoft Active Directory](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/identity/msad/index.md): Back up and restore Active Directory Domain Controllers.
- [Security: Scaleway Secret Manager](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/security/scaleway-sm/index.md): Back up and restore Scaleway Secret Manager secrets.
- [Security: HashiCorp Vault](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/security/vault/index.md): Back up and restore HashiCorp Vault.
- [Service: IMAP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/service/imap/index.md): Back up and restore mailboxes over IMAP.
- [Service: Plakar Control Plane](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/resources/service/pcp/index.md): Back up the configuration and internal database of Plakar Control Plane itself.

### Apps

- [Overview](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/apps/index.md): How source, store and destination apps are set up on resources, and where their fields come from.
- [Source App](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/apps/sources/index.md): How source apps work.
- [Store App](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/apps/stores/index.md): How store apps work, and how to browse restore points.
- [Destination App](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/apps/destinations/index.md): How destination apps work.

### Edges

- [Plakar Edge](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/index.md): Remote executors that run PCP tasks from the network where the resources are.
- [How Edges Work](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/how-edges-work/index.md): How edges connect to PCP, receive tasks, and access secrets.
- [Edge Requirements](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/requirements/index.md): Network access and host tools an edge needs.
- [Edge Enrollment](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/enrollment/index.md): Enable edge enrollment and share edges with child organizations.
- [Edge Installation](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/installation/index.md): Install an edge as a standalone binary, on Kubernetes, or from a custom image.
- [Running Tasks](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/running-tasks/index.md): Run tasks on edges and how PCP selects an edge.
- [Pre-job and Post-job Hooks](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/hooks/index.md): Run scripts on an edge before and after a backup or restore.
- [Supervision and Metrics](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/edges/monitoring/index.md): Health, readiness, and Prometheus metrics endpoints exposed by edges.

### Scheduling

- [Scheduling](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/index.md): Configure one-off and recurring backup, restore, sync, and check tasks using the built-in scheduler.
- [Scheduled Tasks](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/tasks/index.md): The types of tasks PCP runs.
- [One-off Tasks](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/one-off-tasks/index.md): Run a task immediately.
- [Manual Scheduler](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/manual-scheduler/index.md): Attach schedules to tasks.
- [Policy Scheduler](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/policy-scheduler/index.md): How SLA policies schedule tasks automatically.
- [User Schedulers](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/user-schedulers/index.md): Schedulers owned by application users through the API.
- [Job History](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/scheduling/job-history/index.md): Monitor jobs and view their details.

### Access Control

- [Access Control](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/access-control/index.md): Organizations, users, authentication and permissions.
- [Managing Organizations](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/access-control/organizations/index.md): The organization tree, membership, quotas, and switching organizations.
- [Organization Settings](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/access-control/organization-settings/index.md): Per-organization authentication, SMTP, Vector, edge enrollment and webhook settings, and how they are handed down.
- [Managing Users](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/access-control/users/index.md): Member and application users, and API keys.
- [Two-factor Authentication](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/access-control/two-factor-authentication/index.md): Secure accounts with two-factor authentication.
- [Permissions](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/access-control/permissions/index.md): How access is granted, and what each built-in role can reach.

### Compliance

- [Compliance](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/compliance/index.md): Enforce backup requirements, data location and retention obligations, and review activity.
- [SLA Policies](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/compliance/policies/index.md): Define backup SLA requirements (frequency, retention, storage tier) and monitor source compliance against them.
- [Data Residency](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/compliance/residency/index.md): Tie resources to a country, enforce it on every operation, and take signed residency attestations.
- [Legal Hold](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/compliance/legal-hold/index.md): Protect a restore point from deletion or a resource from use, and take signed legal hold attestations.
- [Audit Log](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/compliance/audit-log/index.md): The record of administrative and configuration changes, exportable as a report or a signed sealed archive.

### Operations

- [Control Plane Settings](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/control-plane-settings/index.md): Settings that apply to the whole PCP instance.
- [Email & SMTP](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/email-and-smtp/index.md): Configure SMTP for email notifications.
- [Webhooks](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/webhooks/index.md): Receive PCP events as HTTP requests.
- [Updating Control Plane](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/updating/index.md): Update PCP in place, including air-gapped instances. Requires the Platform Admin or Superuser role.
- [Updating Control Plane AMI on AWS](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/updating/aws/index.md): Update the PCP AMI on AWS.
- [Updating Control Plane QCOW2 on Scaleway](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/updating/scaleway/index.md): Update the PCP image on Scaleway.
- [Updating Control Plane on Proxmox](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/updating/proxmox/index.md): Update the PCP image on Proxmox.
- [Updating Control Plane on vSphere](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/updating/vsphere/index.md): Update the PCP installation on vSphere.
- [Backup and Restore](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/operations/backup-and-restore/index.md): Back up and restore the PCP configuration and data.

### Infrastructure as Code

- [Infrastructure as Code](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/infrastructure-as-code/index.md): Manage PCP declaratively instead of through the web interface.
- [Kubernetes Operator](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/infrastructure-as-code/kubernetes-operator/index.md): Manage stores, sources, destinations, restores and schedules from Kubernetes with plakar-operator.
- [Terraform Provider](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/infrastructure-as-code/terraform/index.md): Manage stores, connectors, schedules, inventories and organizations with the plakarkorp/plakar Terraform provider.
- [Ansible Collection](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/infrastructure-as-code/ansible/index.md): Drive PCP from playbooks with the plakarkorp.plakar Ansible collection.
- [Reference: Kubernetes Operator](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/references/kubernetes-operator/index.md): Field-by-field reference for every custom resource defined by plakar-operator.
- [Reference: Terraform Provider](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/references/terraform-provider/index.md): Argument-by-argument reference for every resource and data source.
- [Reference: Ansible Collection](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/references/ansible-collection/index.md): Option-by-option reference for every module.

### API Reference

- [API v1](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/references/openapi/v1/index.md): Version 1 of the PCP HTTP API, its base URL, authentication and error format. The full OpenAPI schema of the current version is at https://www.plakar.io/openapi.json, and each version is at `/openapi/<version>.json`, for example https://www.plakar.io/openapi/v1.json.

### General guides for Control Plane

- [Automating Backups from an Inventory](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/automated-backups/index.md): Back up the resources of a cloud account with no manual setup per resource: a managed inventory synced every 15 minutes, environment and data class tags set at the provider, a configuration bundle that auto-creates source apps, and SLA policies that schedule the backups.
- [Managing Passphrases](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/managing-passphrases/index.md): How store passphrases work in PCP, how to change one, and what happens when it is forgotten.
- [AWS: IAM Roles, Users & Access Keys](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/aws/iam-users-roles-and-access-keys/index.md): Configure AWS IAM for PCP.
- [Scaleway: IAM Policies & API Keys](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/scaleway/iam-and-api-keys/index.md): Configure Scaleway IAM for PCP.
- [Scaleway: HTTPS Access on a Private Network](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/scaleway/https-access-to-a-private-network/index.md): Deploy PCP on a Scaleway Private Network and reach it over HTTPS.
- [Scaleway: SSH Bastion Access](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/scaleway/ssh-bastion-access/index.md): Reach PCP on a Scaleway Private Network through an SSH bastion.
- [Google Cloud: IAM Roles & Service Accounts](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/google-cloud/iam-roles-and-service-accounts/index.md): Configure Google Cloud IAM for PCP.
- [OVHcloud: API Applications & Credentials](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/ovhcloud/api-keys/index.md): Generate OVHcloud API credentials for PCP.
- [OpenStack: Users & Application Credentials](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/openstack/users-and-application-credentials/index.md): Create an OpenStack user and application credentials with the reader and member roles for PCP.
- [Windows: OpenSSH Server](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/windows/windows-openssh-setup/index.md): Install and configure OpenSSH Server on a Windows host.
- [Kubernetes: Plakar with Kubernetes](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/kubernetes/plakar-with-kubernetes/index.md): The Kubernetes components of the Plakar ecosystem.
- [Kubernetes: Service Accounts and RBAC](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/kubernetes/kubernetes-rbac/index.md): Least-privilege service accounts for the Kubernetes and OpenShift integrations.
- [MTU and Jumbo Frames](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/mtu-and-jumbo-frames/index.md): Ethernet MTU, jumbo frames and TCP MSS, and why they matter for backups.
- [Hosting a Package Repository](https://www.plakar.io/docs/control-plane/guides/self-hosted-package-repository/index.md): Self-hosted repositories for air-gapped PCP instances.
